author: samestrin
body:
## Summary

Sprint 5.0 adds rich quality metrics and Vision AI optimization hints to the DOM extraction feature:

- **QualityMetrics Model**: Exposes 14+ computed values including element counts, visibility ratios, tag analysis, and text statistics
- **VisionAIHints Model**: Provides model compatibility assessments (Claude/Gemini/GPT-4V/Qwen) and tiling recommendations
- **Opt-In Flags**: Keep responses lean by default with `include_metrics` and `include_vision_hints` options
- **Environment Configuration**: Model limits configurable via environment variables
- **JSON Configuration**: Extensible model profiles in `app/vision_model_config.json`

### Key Features

| Feature | Description |
|---------|-------------|
| Quality Metrics | 14 fields: element_count, visible_count, hidden_count, heading_count, unique_tag_count, visible_ratio, hidden_ratio, unique_tags, has_headings, tag_distribution, total_text_length, avg_text_length, min_text_length, max_text_length |
| Vision AI Hints | Model compatibility flags, resize impact percentages, recommended dimensions, tiling recommendations with overlap |
| Model Support | Claude (1568px), Gemini (3072px), GPT-4V (2048px), Qwen-VL (4096px) |
| Configuration | Environment variables (VISION_MODEL_*_MAX_DIMENSION), JSON config file |

### New Files
- `app/vision_model_config.json` - Model profiles configuration
- `docs/vision-ai-optimization.md` - Comprehensive optimization guide

### Modified Files
- `app/models.py` - VisionAIHints and QualityMetrics models
- `app/quality_assessment.py` - Enhanced generate_vision_hints() with all features
- `app/main.py` - Document dimensions for full_page screenshots
- `docs/api-reference.md` - Updated API documentation
- `docs/dom-extraction.md` - Vision AI optimization examples
- `README.md` - Added Vision AI Optimization recipe

- [x] 90% code coverage
- [x] Linting clean (ruff check)
- [x] Docker build verified
- [x] Documentation updated
- [x] Backward compatibility maintained (all flags default to false)

author: dennisgoldfarb
body:
### Motivation
- Generating JavaScript template literals inside Julia string literals produced `ParseError` because `$` was interpreted by Julia during parsing.
- The report generator needs to emit JS template placeholders like `${label}` so they are interpolated at runtime in the browser rather than by Julia.

### Description
- Escape JS template placeholder dollar signs in `julia/metrics_report.jl` so Julia does not try to interpolate them during parsing by replacing `${...}` with `\${...}` in the emitted strings.
- Updated the generated series `name` occurrences to emit ``\${label} · \${speciesLabel}`` so the JS template literal remains intact at runtime.
- Changes are limited to string literals that build the HTML/JS report and do not alter runtime JS logic or data structure.
- Modified file: `julia/metrics_report.jl`.

### Testing
- No automated tests were run.

body:
# This pull request adds an SSO feature as requested in this issue #3376 

# OAuth/OIDC Authentication & Provider Management

This pull request introduces support for OAuth/OIDC authentication, including provider management, secure secret storage, and runtime configuration reloads. It also adds AES-256-GCM encryption for sensitive secrets and integrates these features into the admin server and API.

---

## Key Features

### OAuth/OIDC Configuration
- Adds new configuration options in `config.json` to enable OAuth/OIDC globally.
- Supports multiple providers with independent settings.
- Updates Go configuration structs for dynamic provider handling and validation.

### Admin & API Management
- New endpoints to:
  - List providers
  - Create providers
  - Update providers
  - Delete providers
  - Reload provider configuration without server restarts
- Admin UI updated to display available OAuth providers automatically on the login screen.


### Login Flow Integration
- OAuth login and callback routes added to the admin server.
- Login page dynamically shows providers that are configured in the server.

---

## Secret Encryption

Sensitive OAuth client secrets can now be encrypted using AES-256-GCM.

Behavior based on environment:
- If `GOPHISH_SECRET_KEY` is set: secrets are encrypted before storage.
- If not set: secrets are stored in plaintext (development mode only).

Encryption logic is implemented in `crypto/secrets.go`.

---

## Runtime Reload Support

OAuth providers can be reloaded without restarting the application. This includes:
- Reload endpoints
- Provider lifecycle callbacks
- In-memory state refresh for the admin server

---

## Structural and Dependency Updates
- Updated imports and server initialization to support OAuth provider loading.
- Centralized provider lifecycle management and dependency wiring.
- Adjustments to admin server configuration to support OAuth integration.

---

## Summary

This PR provides the foundation for:
- Secure OAuth/OIDC authentication
- Managed provider lifecycle through API and admin UI
- Encrypted secret handling suitable for production environments
- Dynamic configuration reloads with no downtime

author: joshlebed
body:
# PLP Beat Tracking Service for Lighting Control

This PR implements a real-time beat tracking service using the Predominant Local Pulse (PLP) algorithm. The service detects beats from audio input and provides synchronized output for lighting control systems via OSC and MIDI.

## Key Features

- Real-time audio processing with adaptive beat detection
- Confidence-based state machine for stable beat output
- Multiple output options:
  - OSC messages for QLC+ integration
  - MIDI note output for beat events
  - MIDI clock (24 PPQN) with start/stop messages
- Interactive debug visualization via WebSocket/HTTP server
- Benchmark tool for testing with known-BPM files

## Technical Implementation

- Streaming onset envelope detection for transient analysis
- Autocorrelation-based tempo estimation with adaptive thresholds
- Phase-locked pulse tracking for beat alignment
- Confidence tracking with multiple signal components
- State machine with SEARCHING, LOCKED, and HOLDOVER states

## Usage

```
# Basic usage with OSC output
plp-beat

# Enable MIDI output
plp-beat --midi

# Set BPM range
plp-beat --bpm-min 120 --bpm-max 160

# Debug visualization
plp-beat --debug-server
```

The debug visualization is accessible via web browser at http://localhost:8080/debug.html and provides real-time signal monitoring.

body:
### Motivation

- Make the practice pipeline observable end-to-end with correlated request tracing and structured logs (`requestId`) so failures are diagnosable in Cloudflare tails.  
- Ensure transcription is returned and surfaced to the user even when scoring fails, so users can see “what you said” independently of evaluation.  
- Find and harden the root cause of silent scoring failures by instrumenting STT/LLM network calls and fixing brittle audio encoding on the frontend.  
- Improve UX on the Practice page so transcript, scoring, and actionable errors are clearly separated and include `requestId` for debugging.

### Description

- Added a minimal structured logger in `apps/api/src/utils/logger.ts` exposing `makeRequestId()`, `log()`, `safeTruncate()` and `safeError()` and switched the API to emit JSON logs accessible to Worker tails.  
- Installed a request-tracing Hono middleware in `apps/api/src/app.ts` that attaches `x-request-id`, logs `request.start` / `request.end` / `request.error`, and returns `requestId` on errors.  
- Reworked `POST /api/v1/practice/run` in `apps/api/src/app.ts` to perform staged logging (`input.parse`, `auth/context`, `exercise.load`, `stt.select`, `stt.transcribe`, `llm.select`, `llm.evaluate`, `db.attempt.insert`) with timings and to always return an envelope containing `requestId`, optional `attemptId`, `transcript`, optional `scoring`, and `errors`.  
- Instrumented providers: added HTTP-level timing, truncation and error logging in `apps/api/src/providers/stt.ts` and `apps/api/src/providers/llm.ts`, and changed `selectSttProvider`/`selectLlmProvider` to return provider + health info (`ProviderSelection<T>`).  
- Changed shared types and schemas to support the new envelope: updated `packages/shared/src/types.ts` and `packages/shared/src/schemas.ts` with `PracticeRunResponse`/`practiceRunResponseSchema`.  
- Frontend changes: updated RTK Query `runPractice` type to `PracticeRunResponse` in `apps/web/src/store/api.ts`, replaced fragile `btoa(...new Uint8Array(...))` encoding with a robust `blobToBase64` using `FileReader` in `apps/web/src/pages/PracticePage.tsx`, and added a dedicated Transcript card, error panel (with stage labels), `requestId` footer, and a `Copy transcript` button.  
- Documentation: added a `Debugging practice runs` section to `README.md` describing `wrangler tail` guidance, common failure modes, and a manual test checklist.

### Testing

- Started the frontend dev server with `npm run dev -w apps/web` (Vite) and confirmed the site launched successfully.  
- Ran an automated Playwright script to open `/practice/test` and captured a screenshot of the updated Practice page (artifact available from the run).  
- No automated backend integration tests were executed in this rollout, and no unit tests were added.  
- Manual/workflow validation checklist added to `README.md` for local and Worker modes to reproduce traces via `wrangler tail` and confirm `requestId` propagation.

author: agoodkind
body:
Full page reloads during development were slow and lost browser state like scroll position and form inputs. The live-reload client triggered `window.location.reload()` on every file change, forcing complete page rebuilds even for small template tweaks.

This PR adds hot module replacement using HTMX's morph swap strategy. When template files change, the watcher sends targeted SSE events identifying the changed file. The client maps file paths to DOM targets (`body` for pages, `main` for components) and uses `htmx.ajax()` with `morph:outerHTML` to diff and patch only what changed. CSS and JS changes still trigger full reloads since they require re-execution.

The implementation includes request tracing with sequential swap IDs, consolidated logging that shows file → target → timing in one line, and automatic fallback to full reload when HTMX isn't available. Also bundles HTMX locally instead of using CDN, extracts the inline `theme-init` script to a separate bundled file, and simplifies VSCode launch config to a single Dev Mode compound configuration.

body:
Mobile-Friendly Tables and Enhanced UI

  Summary

  This PR significantly improves the mobile user experience for the tasks and plants tables by implementing responsive design patterns, optimizing column layouts, and enhancing visual clarity on small screens.

  Key Changes

  📱 Mobile Responsive Tables

  - Smart Column Reordering: On mobile devices (< 768px), the tasks table columns are reordered to prioritize the most important information:
    - Mobile order: Date → Notes → Actions → Task → Plant
    - Desktop order: Date → Task → Plant → Notes → Actions
  - Actions Column Repositioned: Moved Actions column to the far right on desktop views for better visual hierarchy
  - Optimized Column Widths:
    - Actions: 65px on mobile, 180px on desktop
    - Date: 75px on mobile
    - Notes: 180px with word wrapping

  📅 Enhanced Date Display

  - Responsive Date Formatting:
    - Desktop: Full format (e.g., "January 13, 2026")
    - Mobile: Abbreviated format (e.g., "Jan 13")
  - Year in Header: On mobile, the year is displayed once in the Date column header (e.g., "Date (2026)") instead of repeating for every row, saving valuable screen space
  - Stacked Date Ranges: Date ranges now display vertically on mobile:
  Jan 20 -
  Jan 27

  ✅ Improved Action Controls

  - Stacked Checkboxes: Complete and Skip checkboxes stack vertically on mobile for better touch targets
  - Stacked Buttons: Plant action buttons (View/Edit/Delete) and bottom action buttons stack vertically on mobile with full width for easier interaction
  - Compact Spacing: Reduced gaps and padding on mobile to maximize content visibility

  🎨 Visual Enhancements

  - Added task type icons for better visual identification:
    - 🌱 Plant seeds
    - 🌿 Observe sprouts
    - 💪 Begin hardening off
    - 🪴 Plant seedlings
    - 🛠️ Garden task
  - Improved table styling with consistent spacing and borders

  🔧 Technical Improvements

  - CSS Media Queries: Comprehensive mobile styles at 768px breakpoint
  - Flexbox Layout: Used CSS flexbox order property for column reordering without changing HTML structure
  - JavaScript Updates: Updated task-row_controller.js to prevent navigation when clicking the Actions column (now last column instead of first)
  - Responsive Utilities: Leveraged Bootstrap's d-md-* classes for show/hide behavior across breakpoints

  Testing

  - ✅ Updated controller tests to handle dual date formats (desktop + mobile)
  - ✅ Fixed calendar view tests to match current UI ("Tasks" header, last frost date location)
  - ✅ Updated system test button text ("+ New Task")
  - ✅ All tests passing

  Files Modified

  - app/frontend/stylesheets/application.css - Added mobile responsive styles
  - app/views/tasks/index.html.erb - Restructured table with responsive date formats and reordered columns
  - app/views/plants/index.html.erb - Added responsive button stacking
  - app/views/plants/show.html.erb - Added responsive button stacking for bottom actions
  - app/frontend/controllers/task-row_controller.js - Updated click handler for new column position
  - app/helpers/tasks_helper.rb - Added task icon helper methods
  - Test files updated to match new implementation

  Browser Compatibility

  - Tested on mobile viewport (< 768px)
  - Desktop view remains unchanged and functional
  - Smooth transition at 768px breakpoint

  Breaking Changes

  None - All changes are additive and maintain backward compatibility

author: jackbayliss
body:
I noticed the `getEventDispatcher()` method can actually return `null`.  I realised after playing with: 
```php 

    DB::connection()->unsetEventDispatcher();
    dd(DB::connection()->getEventDispatcher());
```  

I've adjusted the docblocks for all three classes missing it based on the fact the properties can actually be null:

- [Connection](https://github.com/laravel/framework/blob/6ad8cc987ca9fd2b0402f820b27926464194708a/src/Illuminate/Database/Connection.php#L108-L113)
- [Redis Connection](https://github.com/laravel/framework/blob/6ad8cc987ca9fd2b0402f820b27926464194708a/src/Illuminate/Redis/Connections/Connection.php#L32-L37)
- [Logger ](https://github.com/laravel/framework/blob/6ad8cc987ca9fd2b0402f820b27926464194708a/src/Illuminate/Log/Logger.php#L26-L30) & [Logger allows dispatcher to be null](https://github.com/laravel/framework/blob/6ad8cc987ca9fd2b0402f820b27926464194708a/src/Illuminate/Log/Logger.php#L45) 

This ensures the docblock matches the actual implementation
